summary:
Legal gender recognition in Andorra rests on the Law of the Person and Family of 21 July 2022, which allows trans people to update name and gender on legal documents through a simple process requiring no medical intervention. The same legislation unified civil marriage, so a trans visitor's marital status is recognised under the same regime as everyone else's.

Statutory non-discrimination protection covers gender identity and expression. Law 13/2019 of 15 February 2019 bars discrimination on grounds including gender identity and expression across employment, education, health care, social services, housing and public establishments, and extends that protection specifically to education settings. Bias-motivated offences attract additional penalties. Law 14/2019 of 15 February 2019 on the rights of children and adolescents establishes that transgender children must be respected in their gender identity.

Andorran police recorded an average of two to three bias-motivated incidents each month during 2025. The association DiversAnd flagged further incidents across the June Pride celebrations and has called for a formal system to register and classify bias-motivated violence, so that such acts can be recognised and prosecuted as hate crime. No such registration system was in place during the year.

Access to gender-affirming care is a live question. In August 2023 DiversAnd met the Ministry of Health to press for protocols covering puberty blockers and hormone therapy for 16-year-olds, and in some cases for 14-year-olds, following regulatory changes made in 2022. The sources in hand do not establish whether those protocols have since been issued, so a visitor seeking continuing care should confirm arrangements in advance.

Hostile media output occurs and is contested. A transphobic opinion piece in El Periòdic d'Andorra on 27 September 2023 was removed online with a public apology after DiversAnd requested it, though the piece had already run in print.

Public LGBT expression is lawful and has a visible history. The first LGBT demonstration was held on 6 September 2002 and the first gay pride parade followed on 23 June 2003 at Plaça del Poble in Andorra la Vella, organised by the association Som Com Som; DiversAnd was formed in 2019 after Som Com Som ended its work in 2018 and organised a pride parade that June.
tangentialFactors:
Andorra's head of government, Xavier Espot Zamora, who has held office since 2019, came out publicly as gay in September 2023, stating that he had never hidden it, a signal of the wider social climate in which he continues to serve as prime minister.

The Ministry of Equality implemented equality measures during 2025, and the Department of Equality launched the short film #lovingdiversity on 17 May 2019 to raise online awareness of LGBT lives.

Civil union has been available since the 2014 law, and adoption has been open to same-sex couples since that law. Same-sex sexual activity has been legal since the prohibiting statute was abolished in 1791, and the age of consent is 16 under Penal Code Article 206 for both same-sex and heterosexual relationships (Wikipedia cites Articles 162 and 163).

Violence against LGBT people has a documented history. In 2000 a 17-year-old gay man, Nuno Ribeiro, was murdered in the country because of his sexual orientation, prompting public outcry, and reports exist of parents expelling their children from home over sexual orientation.

GayLawNet's Andorra page indexes civil unions, discrimination, hate crimes, marriage, sodomy and trans legal status but carries a 'limited information' marking, so its entries should be corroborated against the primary statutes.
localsOnly:
Residents benefit from the document-change procedure established by the Family Law of 21 July 2022, which permits name and gender marker updates on legal documents without any medical or surgical requirement.

Law 14/2019 obliges that transgender children be respected in their gender identity, and Law 13/2019 extends non-discrimination protection, including gender identity and expression, into education settings. Preventing and addressing bullying and discrimination in schools is a stated focus of DiversAnd's work.

Residents in same-sex relationships have had access to civil union since 2014 and to joint adoption since the same year, and marriage since the 2022 law unified the regime.

For residents, care remains the contested area: the 2023 request to the Ministry of Health for puberty-blocker and hormone protocols covering 16-year-olds and, in some cases, 14-year-olds has not been shown as resolved in the sources held here.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether gender-affirming care protocols covering puberty blockers and hormone therapy for 16- and 14-year-olds were actually adopted after the August 2023 meeting with the Ministry of Health is unresolved in the sources held here.

The formal system for registering and classify bias-motivated violence that DiversAnd called for in 2025 is not recorded as established; equally, the police figure of two to three bias-motivated incidents per month is not broken down by the type of bias involved, so the share attributable to trans victims is not sourced.

No source in this inventory addresses entry or visa screening, border questions about gender markers, or any risk of involuntary disclosure during immigration processing for Andorra; the Schengen-adjacent arrangements that would govern this are not covered by the materials assembled.

Nothing here is sourced on facilities access, health-care treatment of trans visitors, or recognition of foreign gender documents for short-term stays. GayLawNet's page on Andorra carries a 'limited information' flag, which limits its value for verification.
